ambiguities.description: The deal says '85/15 after expenses' but does not state whether the 85% is applied after the capped expenses (i.e., actuals limited to $1,150) or after actual expenses regardless of the cap. If actuals exceed $1,150, these produce different artist payouts.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated after the capped expense amount ($1,150 maximum), even if actuals are higher
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable. If actuals are, say, $1,400, artist still nets as if only $1,150 was deducted, gaining ~$212 (85% of $250 difference).

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated after actual expenses, with the cap serving only as a ceiling the venue committed not to exceed
plausibleReadings.impact: Neutral in practice if venue honors the cap, but leaves open a dispute if venue submits actuals above $1,150.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Can you confirm: is the 85% applied against gross minus the capped $1,150 (regardless of actual expenses), or against gross minus actual expenses up to the $1,150 ceiling?

ambiguities.description: It is not stated whether the $600 hospitality cap is included within the $1,150 expense cap or sits outside it as a separate line item.

plausibleReadings.summary: Hospitality is a sub-category of the $1,150 expense cap, meaning total venue deductions are capped at $1,150 including hospitality
Hospitality is a separate cap stacked on top of the $1,150 expense cap, allowing up to $1,750 in total deductions
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable. Could reduce artist net by up to $510 extra (85% of $600) versus reading p1.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Is the $600 hospitality cap a sub-item within the $1,150 expense cap, or is it an additional allowance on top of the $1,150?
